proposal.utterance: What kind of BFO entity is the disposition to recognize authority?

entities.label: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority
entities.rationale: The disposition to recognize authority is an internally grounded tendency of an agent (typically a legal official or citizen) to treat certain commands or norms as authoritative. BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016) captures internally grounded realizable entities — capacities or tendencies that inhere in a bearer and may or may not be realized. This fits better than Role (externally grounded) because the disposition is a psychological/doxastic tendency intrinsic to the bearer, not an externally conferred social position. It is not a Quality (BFO_0000019) because it is a realizable capacity rather than a static measurable property. It differs from working:ActorWill (also BFO_0000016) in that it is specifically directed toward authority recognition rather than general volitional capacity.

relations.rationale: DispositionToRecognizeAuthority is a subclass of BFO Disposition, as it is an internally grounded realizable entity inhering in an agent.

open_questions: Should DispositionToRecognizeAuthority be further refined as a subclass of working:ActorWill, or kept as a sibling subclass of BFO_0000016?
Is this disposition intended to inhere in individual persons (officials, citizens), collective agents (institutions), or both?
Should we distinguish a disposition to recognize authority in general from a disposition to recognize a specific kind of authority (e.g., legal vs. moral authority)?
Is the user asking a classificatory question (what type is it?) without intending to assert a new ontological commitment — in which case no new entity need be added to the graph?
proposal.rationale_summary: The disposition to recognize authority is best typed as a BFO Disposition (BFO_0000016): an internally grounded realizable entity that inheres in a bearer (a person or collective) and is realized in processes of deference, compliance, or acknowledgment of authority. It is internally grounded (the bearer has it as a standing tendency) rather than externally conferred (which would make it a Role), and it is a capacity rather than a static measurable property (which would make it a Quality). A new class DispositionToRecognizeAuthority is proposed as a subclass of BFO_0000016. However, since the user asked a classificatory question rather than asserting a new entity, this proposal is tentative pending confirmation that the user wants the class added to the working ontology.
